function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

I don’t have a way to probe your connection from here, so I can’t tell you the exact download/upload speeds right now. But you can check it yourself in a few quick ways: | Method | How to do it | |--------|--------------| | **Web browser** | Visit (or ) and click “Go” / “Start Test.” The page will show your download, upload, and ping. | | **Windows PowerShell** | If you have the free *Speedtest CLI* tool installed, open PowerShell and run:
`speedtest-cli --simple`
This prints a concise summary. | | **Command‑line (Linux/macOS)** | Install the CLI (`sudo apt install speedtest-cli` or `brew install speedtest-cli`) and run:
`speedtest-cli --simple` | | **Mobile app** | Download the official Speedtest app from Google Play or the App Store and tap “Go.” | If you’d like me to run a command on your Windows machine (e.g., to launch the Speedtest CLI), just let me know and I’ll use the `cmd_controller_execute` tool. Otherwise, the web‑browser method is the quickest and works on any device.
